verdict.rationale: kitty documents a remote-control interface that lets scripts open windows, send text to any window and retitle windows and tabs. A hands-on runtime probe confirmed a complete external control loop: `kitten @ ls` returned JSON state, and send-text, get-text and close-window all worked over a listen socket. missing for 10: evidence in the pack detailing the underlying wire/JSON protocol specification beyond the CLI command surface.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: kitty can be controlled from scripts or the shell prompt. You can open new windows, send arbitrary text input to any window, change the title of windows and tabs, etc.

`kitten @ ls` returned full window/tab/layout state as JSON, `kitten @ send-text "echo PA_PROBE_OK"` executed in the live window, `kitten @ get-text` read the output back, `kitten @ close-window` tore it down — complete external agent-control loop verified hands-on.
Control it from scripts or the shell
